Chaweng is Koh Samui's party centre: free beach fire shows and DJs at ARKbar every night from 20:00, the clubs on Soi Green Mango until about 04:00, and weekend pool parties at the beach clubs. Fisherman's Village and Bang Rak do sunset beach clubs, Lamai does pubs and bands. The biggest nights are on Koh Phangan, 30–50 minutes away by boat: the Full Moon Party (next on 24 November, 24 December and 31 December 2026), the Half Moon Festival and the jungle parties. Our shared Full Moon boat costs 1,400 THB return with hotel pickup from most areas.

We have run party boats between Samui and Koh Phangan since 2006, and this page is the planner we wish every guest read first: what's on each night, which parties are worth the crossing, what the law says about alcohol and drugs, what a night costs and how to get home in one piece. For bars and late food street by street, see Chaweng nightlife and Lamai nightlife; for every dated event, the party calendar 2026–2027.

Chaweng: the party centre

Most of Samui's partying happens on a 2 km strip of Chaweng between the beach road and the sand. The night usually runs in three acts: a sunset drink and the free fire show on the beach, dinner and a live band on Chaweng Beach Road, then the clubs after midnight.

  • ARKbar Beach Club: open daily from about 10:00 to 02:00, with a free fire show and DJs on the sand from about 20:00 to 24:00. Pool parties are listed for Wednesday and Friday, 14:00–19:00. Adults only after about 21:00.
  • Soi Green Mango: the club lane. The Green Mango Club is open nightly from about 21:00 to 04:00, with two dance floors over several open-air levels; it is empty before 23:00 and full from about 00:30. Entry is usually free; you must be 20 with ID.
  • Elephant Beach Club: fire shows most nights and Saturday DJs until about 03:00.
  • Bar Solo and the beach-road bars: live cover bands most nights from about 21:00.
  • Paris Follies Cabaret: drag cabaret on Chaweng Beach Road, daily from about 19:00, entry with a drink.

Honest notes: Chaweng is loud, touts work every corner of Soi Green Mango, drink prices are two to three times the 7-Eleven price, and late taxis are unmetered and expensive. Saturday is the peak night; Monday and Tuesday are quiet. Street-by-street guide: Chaweng nightlife.

Fisherman's Village, Bang Rak and the north coast

The north coast is where Samui goes for sunset. Bang Rak and Plai Laem, near Big Buddha, have a cluster of beach clubs with west-facing views across to Koh Phangan: Chi Samui, Tembo, Malika and 79 Beach Club, which runs themed nights and sells day passes. Fisherman's Village in Bophut is calmer: Friday's walking street from about 17:00 to 23:00, cocktails in beach-front bars and Coco Tam's fire shows on the sand, with most places winding down by midnight. It is the best part of the island for a lively evening and a quiet night's sleep. See Fisherman's Village Walking Street and Big Buddha Beach.

Lamai and Maenam nights

Lamai, 20–25 minutes south of Chaweng, swaps clubs for pubs and bands: Shamrock Irish Pub's nightly show band (about 21:30–01:30), reggae at Rock Bar by the Hin Ta and Hin Yai rocks, fire shows at Teddy Weed until about 02:00 and a beer-bar quarter behind the beach road. Beer is cheaper, at about 80–120 THB. Maenam on the north coast is quiet except for Cape Away's Sunday party, open about 10:00–22:00. Details: Lamai nightlife and Maenam.

Full Moon Party from Samui

The Full Moon Party on Haad Rin Sunrise Beach, Koh Phangan, is the biggest beach party in Thailand, with tens of thousands of people, a dozen sound systems along the sand, fire shows and buckets of drinks from dusk until after sunrise. There is no Full Moon Party on Samui itself; you cross by boat. Dates are set by the Haad Rin organisers and move off Buddhist holidays, when alcohol sales are banned:

Boat options from Samui

  • Shared Full Moon speedboat: 1,400 THB per person return (1,800 THB on New Year's Eve), with hotel pickup from most areas, departures between 18:00 and 23:00 and return boats through the night. Lipa Noi, Nathon, Taling Ngam, Bang Kao and Thong Krut add 400 THB per person return.
  • Private Full Moon speedboat: for up to 10 guests, 19,500 THB one way or 35,800 THB return at your own times.
  • Public ferry: the Haad Rin Queen and other ferries run from Big Buddha pier, but late-night returns are limited and crowded, and you still need transfers at both ends.

We don't sell Full Moon Party entry: it is about 200 THB, paid at the gate in Haad Rin. Step-by-step planning, safety and what to bring: Full Moon Party from Koh Samui.

Half Moon Festival from Samui

The Half Moon Festival in Ban Tai, Koh Phangan, is a more produced, ticketed electronic music event than the Full Moon: a beach-club day party, then the "Magic Forest" night in the Ban Tai jungle from about 21:00 to sunrise. In 2026 tickets cost about 1,300 THB for the day party, 2,500 THB for the Magic Forest night and 4,900 THB for VIP.

Jungle, Waterfall and other Koh Phangan parties

  • Jungle Experience, Ban Tai: the night before the Full Moon, about 22:00–06:00, age 20+ with ID. 2026 dates: Mon 23 Nov, Wed 23 Dec (Christmas edition) and Wed 30 Dec.
  • Waterfall Party: an open-air jungle venue with several stages around a stream, 21:00 to sunrise. November 2026 dates: Wed 11, Sun 22 and Thu 26 Nov.
  • OXA jungle party, near Ban Tai: mostly Fridays. Our OXA package from Samui costs 2,500 THB per person with hotel pickup from about 22:00, the shared speedboat, minivans on Phangan and entry, back at 05:00. Dates: 6, 13, 20 and 27 Nov; 4, 11, 18, 25 and 29 Dec 2026; 8, 15, 19 and 29 Jan; 5, 12 and 19 Feb 2027.
  • Utopia, Thong Nai Pan: an electronic night on Phangan's north-east coast. Our Utopia package is 3,900 THB with boat and entry; dates on request. The crossing to Thong Nai Pan is the most exposed to the monsoon swell from October to December.

All Phangan parties are adults only and check ID. More on what's on across the water: our sister site KohPhangan.com.

New Year's Eve, Christmas and Loy Krathong

  • Loy Krathong, Tue 24 Nov 2026: the festival of floating krathong baskets on water, at Chaweng Lake, Big Buddha and the beaches. It falls on the same night as the Full Moon Party, so you can float a krathong at sunset and take the boat to Haad Rin later. Sky lanterns are banned on Samui. See Loy Krathong on Koh Samui.
  • Christmas Eve, Thu 24 Dec 2026: also a Full Moon Party night, plus resort dinners on Samui. The Jungle Experience Christmas edition is the night before.
  • New Year's Eve, Thu 31 Dec 2026: a free countdown with concerts and fireworks at Central Samui in Chaweng (the 2026 programme was not yet published at the start of November), a beach countdown at ARKbar (free before 21:00 and 500 THB after in 2025), fireworks along Chaweng, Fisherman's Village, Lamai, Maenam and Choeng Mon, and resort galas such as Anantara Bophut's at 14,500++ THB per person. Across the water, the NYE Full Moon Party; our shared boat is 1,800 THB that night.

Popular NYE parties and dinners sell out by mid-December. Full guide: Christmas and New Year's Eve on Koh Samui.

Songkran: the biggest street party

Thai New Year, Songkran, is a public holiday on 13–15 April 2027, and on Samui the water fights usually start on 12 April. Chaweng Beach Road turns into the island's main water-fight street, with pickup trucks of water barrels, music and powder; Lamai and Nathon hold their own events. In 2025 ARKbar ran several nights of free beach parties, SEEN a pool party and Central Samui a foam party from 12:00 to 24:00, and similar programmes are expected in 2027. Keep your phone in a waterproof pouch, don't ride a scooter (road accidents peak nationally over Songkran) and don't throw water at monks, the elderly or anyone in a vehicle with the windows down. See Songkran on Koh Samui.

A three-night party plan

  1. Night 1 (Friday) Fisherman's Village Walking Street from 18:00, Coco Tam's fire show at 21:00, then a Grab to Chaweng for ARKbar and Soi Green Mango.
  2. Day 2 Sleep in. Late lunch, then the CLUB SEEN pool party or a beach-club daybed in Bang Rak for sunset.
  3. Night 2 (Saturday) Muay Thai at Phetchbuncha from 21:00, then Elephant Beach Club or the clubs until late.
  4. Day 3 A gentle boat day: the Pig Island sunset tour (1,550 THB adult) from Thong Krut.
  5. Night 3 If it is a Full Moon night, the shared boat to Haad Rin; otherwise Cape Away's Sunday party in Maenam or a quiet night.

Rules and the law

  • Alcohol hours: since 29 May 2026 shops may sell alcohol from 11:00 to 24:00; the old afternoon ban has ended. Hotels and licensed entertainment venues are exempt and may stay open until about 02:00–04:00 depending on zoning and licence.
  • Drinking age: 20. Clubs and the Phangan parties check ID.
  • Holy-day bans: on Buddhist holy days shops and 7-Eleven can't sell alcohol, but hotels, licensed bars and entertainment venues in tourist areas may still serve. There are no ban days in November or December 2026. The 2027 bans are Sun 21 Feb, Thu 20 May, 18–19 July (one source says a day later) and about 15 October.
  • Drugs: penalties are severe and police run checks around party nights, including at piers. Cannabis needs a prescription to buy, and smoking it in public can bring a fine of up to 25,000 THB.
  • Vapes: illegal in Thailand, for tourists too: confiscation, fines and possible detention.
  • No alcohol at temples, petrol stations, public parks or on public transport.

Full legal detail: drugs and alcohol law on Koh Samui.

Getting home safely

  • Plan the ride before you go out: Grab works best in Chaweng, Bophut and Lamai, with surge pricing after 02:00 and in rain. Taxis are unmetered, so agree the fare first; expect 20–30 % more at night. Songthaews stop by about 22:00.
  • Never ride after drinking: Samui's roads are dark, hilly and full of drunk riders at night. Insurance won't pay out for drink-riding.
  • Drink spiking: the UK Foreign Office warns of spiking and sexual assault in island party areas. Watch your drink being made, keep it with you and look after friends.
  • Party boats: there are no public boats back from Koh Phangan in the middle of the night, so book a return before you go, and only board licensed boats with life jackets.
  • The sea: don't swim at night or drunk; rip currents run off Chaweng and Lamai from October to December.
  • Emergency numbers: Tourist Police 1155 · Police 191 · Ambulance 1669.

See getting around Koh Samui, scams to avoid and the Tourist Police.

A big night in Chaweng costs most people 1,500–2,000 THB; a Full Moon night from Samui, with the boat, entry, drinks and food, about 3,000–4,000 THB. Prices rise 10–20 % from mid-December to February. See Koh Samui on a budget.

Where to stay for parties

For big nights, stay in central Chaweng within walking distance of Soi Green Mango, so you never need a ride home at 04:00; north Chaweng and Chaweng Noi are quieter and a few minutes away. Bophut and Fisherman's Village suit couples who want beach clubs and the Friday market with quiet nights. Lamai suits pubs-and-bands people. All of these are inside our standard pickup zone for the Full Moon boat. Compare areas: where to stay on Koh Samui and Chaweng vs Lamai.

Groups, birthdays and stag or hen parties

Groups of six or more do best with something private. A private Full Moon speedboat for up to 10 costs 35,800 THB return, which is about 3,600 THB each with your own departure and return times. For a birthday or a stag or hen day, a sunset charter on the Beat Boat, a junk or a catamaran gives you a party with a captain and no neighbours. Book beach-club cabanas ahead for Saturdays and holidays. Tell us your date, group size and budget on WhatsApp and we quote in writing; private charters are paid in THB by secure link. Our full fleet: Koh Samui boat charter.

Koh Samui or Koh Phangan for parties?

Samui has a party every night of the week, better hotels and restaurants and an airport, but its clubs are mainstream. Koh Phangan has the headline parties (Full Moon, Half Moon, the jungle nights) and a stronger underground scene, but quiet normal nights outside Haad Rin and Ban Tai and basic transport. Many people stay on Samui and cross for one or two party nights by boat, which is exactly what our party boats are for. Compare the islands: Koh Samui vs Koh Phangan vs Koh Tao.
